review_scope: Bounded source/assertion review. Parent findings and gate-results supersede draft/run status. Neither whole-clause nor all-feature certification.

features.source_location: Effective ISO printed pp. 530–532 (physical pp. 545–547): §12.7.4.1 states that inheritance range shall not be limited; Table 226 marks /FT, /Ff, /V and /DV inheritable. EC3 Issue #28 amends /T requiredness; #313 narrows AA's annotation cross-reference; neither changes these inherited entries. Issue #683 removes 'inheritable' from ResetForm action /Flags, not field attributes.
features.normative_effect: A field gets an inheritable entry from the nearest ancestor that states it; readers cannot impose a fixed chain-depth limit. A terminal field may therefore obtain type, flags, current value and reset default from different ancestors. /V and /DV belong to the field and may differ among terminal descendants where a descendant overrides an inherited entry.
assertions: crates/pdf-model/src/form.rs::a_fields_type_flags_and_value_come_from_the_ancestor_that_states_them asserts public FormField FT/Ff/V two field links above a widget
features.test_changes_since_prior: The above inheritance tests are not changed in 4015a9ae..b901326c. New max_len_model.rs tests exercise inherited /MaxLen in import and calculation paths, but inspect field_value and saved /V rather than the generated public appearance.
features.verdict: The general parent-chain implementation has direct unit and public appearance evidence. I found no standalone current execution evidence in this shard. The new exact-xref fixture uses two terminal fields under one nonterminal parent (not two widgets belonging to one field): both inherit the same ancestor /V, while the second terminal field overrides /DV. Full reset has distinct expected results per terminal field. Current write_resets delegates storage to holder, which chooses the ancestor that held the original /V; the second child's different default can then overwrite the shared ancestor value. Separate runtime and saved/reopened tests isolate the persistence claim. This is a concrete likely serialization defect, not a claim that inheritance itself is incomplete.
residuals: The drafts have not been compiled or executed by this agent; parent owns execution.
The draft tests full-form reset, not Table 242 inclusion/exclusion descendant targeting; EC3 #174 specifically amends the exclusion branch and remains outside this result.
The two-child reset behavior should also be checked for a later user edit and import; this shard does not assert those variants.

features.source_location: Effective ISO §12.7.2 printed p. 528 / physical p. 543 says a merged field/widget appearance shall agree with its current value and notes variable text may need dynamic appearances. §12.7.6.3 printed p. 555 / physical p. 570 says selected fields shall have /V set to /DV or /V removed when no default exists.
features.normative_effect: A reset changes the field value to its effective default, and any appearance provided for the widget must agree with the value. Saving must not leave a shared ancestor /V that makes sibling fields disagree with their distinct effective /DV values.
features.test_changes_since_prior: These reset assertions are unchanged since 4015a9ae. They use a merged single-widget field with local /V and /DV, so they do not distinguish a shared inherited /V from per-terminal inherited defaults. Draft inherited_reset_value_appearance.rs uses a valid explicit xref, asserts no recovery, independent first/second effective defaults, public field values, visible generated text, and saved/reopened values and drawing.
features.verdict: Existing tests demonstrate ordinary reset ordering and save behavior, but not the multi-terminal ancestor-storage interaction. Code inspection identifies a likely defect in write_resets/holder for siblings that inherit the same old /V and have different effective defaults. The runtime draft and separate save/reopen draft give a precise counterexample to the ledger's broad saved-file sentence. No execution claim is made.
residuals: After parent execution, inspect serialized dictionaries to ensure the fix writes a terminal override for only the child whose /DV differs; a runtime-only pass would not establish persisted consistency.

features.source_location: §12.7.8.3.2 printed pp. 577–579 / physical pp. 592–594 states that imported FDF entries replace corresponding field entries of the same fully qualified name; Table 232 defines /MaxLen as the maximum length of field text. Scope is corroborated by doc/questions/A834 item 1 and ADR 2840; scripts that mutate document values/appearance properties are within the 2026-10-08 ratification in doc/scope-ratifications.md, while external effects remain excluded.
features.normative_effect: Import replacement and truncation are required in the owner-ratified product behavior; Table 232 alone does not prescribe the exact replacement policy for overlong programmatic input. A value displayed after a replacement should not continue to show stale field artwork.
features.test_changes_since_prior: forms_data.rs and value_statements.rs assertions are unchanged in 4015a9ae..b901326c. max_len_model.rs is new and asserts field_value and/or saved /V for user-set, imported, and calculated overlength values; it does not assert that the generated page appearance contains the same truncated value. The only change in variable_text.rs is a nested BMC/EMC assertion unrelated to form values.
features.verdict: Import replacement has public drawing and stored-appearance assertions. `/MaxLen` entry paths are new and value/save assertions are meaningful; no direct source-derived failure was found. A small residual is that new truncation tests do not assert page output after the cut. Scope ratification does not excuse values/appearance inconsistency; no excluded side effect is implicated.
residuals: No exact-xref, no-recovery assertion appears inside max_len_model.rs; its hand-built PDF uses an explicit xref but that condition is not independently asserted.
No test in the new module asserts generated page text after truncation for set/import/calculation.
